headline: Record quarter as margin widens and credit costs reverse
summary_short: Third Federal (TFSL) posted record net income of $30.5M for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, up 31.4% q/q and 42.0% y/y, as net interest margin rose to 1.90% and diluted EPS climbed to $0.11 (+37.5% q/q and y/y).
summary_long: Net income rose 31.4% q/q and 42.0% y/y to a record $30.5M, driven by higher net interest income, a $3.5M provision release, higher non-interest income, and lower non-interest expense. Net interest income grew 4.6% q/q to $81.4M as the earning-asset yield rose faster than funding costs, lifting NIM to 1.90% (+6bps q/q). Non-interest expense fell 2.3% q/q on lower salary and benefit costs. Total assets grew 3.4% q/q to $18.08B; deposits fell 1.9% to $9.99B as CDs ran off amid competitive pricing, offset by borrowed-funds growth. Stockholders' equity rose to $1,957.4M. Capital ratios remain well above well-capitalized thresholds (CET1/Tier1 16.88%, Tier1 leverage 10.72%). No numeric forward guidance was given.

drivers.explanation: Higher net interest income, a release of provision for credit losses, higher non-interest income, and lower non-interest expense all contributed.
A nine-bp rise in earning-asset yield (mainly loans) outpaced a five-bp rise in the cost of interest-bearing liabilities, widening the spread.
Interest rate spread improved four bps to 1.58%, lifting margin six bps to 1.90%.
Salaries and benefits fell $1.8M on lower group health costs and higher capitalized payroll for loan origination and software work.
CDs fell $220.9M amid competitive deposit pricing as the company managed funding costs against customer-attrition risk.
Increase attributed to normal fluctuations and liquidity management, per the filing; no further detail given.
CEO cited record $30.5M quarterly earnings, over $600M of first-mortgage originations, NIM up to 1.90%, a 10.72% Tier 1 capital ratio, and a core banking-system upgrade.
